title: Isolated I-O
body:
The alternative to [[Memory Mapping]]. Device registers live in their own address space,
separate from main memory, and are reached with dedicated instructions (`IN` / `OUT` on
x86) plus an extra bus line saying which space this address refers to.

| | [[Memory Mapping]] | **Isolated I/O** |
|---|---|---|
| Address space | Shared with memory | Separate |
| Instructions | Ordinary loads and stores | Dedicated I/O instructions |
| Cost | Sacrifices main memory address space | Needs extra instructions, extra bus signal, more complex CPU |
| Programming | Any pointer operation works on a device register | I/O code cannot use normal C pointers |

The [[Motorola 68000]] is memory-mapped, which is why everything in this course reads and
writes device registers as if they were variables.
